gaps.quote: turns a vector into its Fourier coefficients
gaps.note: The page uses 'Fourier coefficients' in its opening sentence without explaining it or linking it. The profile excludes Fourier machinery, and the later definition gives the entries of the transform but never says they are the Fourier coefficients.

gaps.quote: it splits $u$ into its even- and odd-indexed entries and transforms each half at length $q/2$
gaps.note: The page never says what the half-length transforms compute (the same transform with root omega squared is not stated) or how their two results are combined into the entries of the full transform. So the claim that the FFT computes the transform in O(q log q) operations cannot be checked from the page. 'Operations' is also not defined (arithmetic on complex numbers or bit operations).

The O(q) term is the cost of the combining step, which the page does not describe, so the recurrence cannot be derived from the page. No base case is given. Solving the recurrence to O(q log q) is followable with the profile's recurrences, but the recurrence itself is asserted.
